svg.title: Benchmark Panel A: score and answer length for four Claude tiers, three ways
svg.desc: Panel A, run of 2026-07-01: the same four Claude models answered the same 15 tasks three ways, the task alone, the task plus a be-concise line, and the task plus the Fabius rules, scored blind out of 15 by two judges. Fable 5: score 14.50, 14.60, 14.73; average length 3087, 1649, 2307 characters. Sonnet 5: score 14.07, 14.07, 14.50; average length 3699, 1606, 2452 characters. Opus 4.8: score 14.40, 14.43, 14.60; average length 3570, 1274, 2855 characters. Haiku 4.5: score 11.73, 12.43, 11.40; average length 4111, 2454, 2653 characters. Fabius answers were 20.0 to 35.5 percent shorter than the task alone on every tier; the be-concise line was shorter still on every tier. Haiku 4.5 scored lower with Fabius. The two judges differ by 0.72 of 15 on average: read the score gaps as small. Measured in July 2026 before Fabius 3.x existed. Data: evals/results.v5.json.
svg.text: PANEL A · RUN OF 2026-07-01 · FOUR CLAUDE TIERS
Shorter answers on all four tiers, a higher score on three
Same model, same 15 tasks, three ways. Two judges scored every answer blind.
The plain “be concise” line wrote shorter still, on every tier.
The two judges differ by 0.72 of 15 on average: read the score gaps as small.
Measured in July 2026 before Fabius 3.x existed. Data: evals/results.v5.json.
